title: Create per-endpoint quality profile schema and automated error-budget reclamation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently have coarse endpoint availability and latency SLOs but no standardized schema for per-model quality SLI definitions (e.g., promptset-based accuracy, hallucination rate, top-k semantic match). This makes it hard to (1) attribute quality regressions to specific model variants, (2) automate error-budget reclamation when a model is downgraded, and (3) enact graded circuit-breaker escalation tied to quality burn rather than only latency/availability.

Goal: Define a compact, machine-readable per-endpoint 'Quality Profile' schema that describes the canonical SLIs for an endpoint/model (latency percentiles, availability, promptset pass-rate, hallucination ceiling, semantic-divergence threshold). Build an automated 'Error-Budget Reclamation' playbook that:
- maps burn-rate thresholds to actions (alert, soft-evict->fallback variant, hard circuit-break),
- integrates with multi-region routing to preferentially re-route traffic to healthy regions/variants,
- documents operator steps and automated remediation runbooks to reclaim budget safely.

Scope: schema design, mapping to existing metrics in Prometheus/Cloudwatch, alert rules, circuit-breaker escalation matrix, an automation job (Lambda/K8s operator) to enact graded traffic shifts, and a human-facing runbook for on-call. This ticket outputs a schema RFC, dashboard templates, a stub operator prototype, and the final runbook.

Non-goals: Changing model training/eval tooling, deep research into new quality metrics (we will encode existing promptset metrics and semantic similarity scores).
acceptance_criteria: A documented JSON Schema for 'Quality Profile' that can be attached to endpoints and model-variants
Mapping table from schema fields to metric names and queries (Prometheus and runtime telemetry)
A policy matrix that ties error-budget burn-rate bands to automated actions (soft eviction, degrade to cached response, circuit-break) and required human approvals
An automated prototype (k8s job or serverless) able to shift 10%/50%/100% traffic to fallback variants given simulated burn signals
Runbook with play-by-play steps for on-call to follow when quality SLOs are breached, including postmortem checklist and rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes added; spoke with PM (J. Huang) to align on customer-impact tiers. PM asked for 'low-friction fallbacks' for PLG customers. Link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/prd/quality-profiles

2026-02-18 - Luca Martinez: Initial draft of schema posted in RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/87. Core fields: latency.p95_ms, availability.5xx_rate, promptset.pass_rate, hallucination.rate, semantic.similarity.p50. Need review from telemetry and eval teams.

2026-02-22 - Telemetry review (N. O'Connor): Suggested renaming promptset.pass_rate -> eval.promptset.success_rate and standardizing units for similarity (cosine * 100). We accepted suggestion and updated RFC.

2026-02-28 - Design feedback (M. Rivera): Request to include human-readable 'degradation_intent' label (e.g., preserve-latency-origin, preserve-quality-origin) so console can explain fallback behavior to customers. Added to schema.

2026-03-03 - Reliability review (SRE): Proposed burn-rate bands: <1x (monitor), 1-4x (alert + canary fallback 10%), 4-10x (automatic 50% soft-evict to fallback model), >10x (hard circuit-break to fallback region/variant). We incorporated the 50% step to reduce blast radius.

2026-03-07 - Luca Martinez: Prototype operator implemented to read Quality Profile and execute traffic shift using the routing API (internal RFC GA-32). Demoed to SRE and PM; follow-ups: add dry-run logs and more conservative default time windows for evaluation (5m->15m window).

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Updated runbook with incident play and postmortem template. Plan to open implementation tickets for productionization and add dashboards: ENG-55679 (dashboard templates), ENG-55680 (operator hardening).
